title: Grove imposes key-hygiene requirements on Delegates and makes a 48-hour compromise response grounds for removal
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.7.1 obliges Delegates to sign votes from "a hardware wallet or an equivalent secure device," to "use **unique signing keys that are never reused for personal transactions**," and to enable MFA on any platform accounts used for governance communication.

The key-reuse prohibition is the substantive one. A hardware wallet protects the key; key separation limits what a compromise reaches. A delegate signing governance votes with a wallet they also use to interact with arbitrary contracts exposes Grove's governance to every risk that wallet takes on — a malicious approval in an unrelated transaction becomes a governance incident. Separation makes the delegate's personal risk-taking their own problem.

The response procedure at A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.7.2 is a three-step containment: the Delegate notifies the Foundation on discovery; the Foundation flags the registry entry "Suspended - Security Review," notifies the Forum, and annuls all voting power to the address; the Delegate may then submit a new verified address, and on approval "delegations migrate at the next snapshot-block." Migration is the notable detail — recovery restores the *existing* delegations to a new address rather than requiring every delegator to redelegate, which is a materially better outcome than the offboarding path offers.

A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.7.3 supplies the enforcement: failing to execute those steps "within **48 hours** constitutes grounds for emergency removal."

The 48-hour clock is doing something specific. The dangerous interval in a key compromise is between the delegate realizing and the system reacting, and that interval depends entirely on self-reporting — nobody else can observe it. Attaching removal to the delay rather than to the compromise itself makes concealment costlier than disclosure, which is the only lever available for a fact only the delegate knows.
description: Delegates must sign from hardware wallets with keys never reused for personal transactions and MFA on governance accounts;
